results.name: How to Download a Digital Item
results.title: How to Download a Digital Item
results.body:
Quick answer

Digital items you’ve purchased can be viewed and downloaded from the Purchases section of your Etsy account.

If you have questions about an item or order, your seller is the best person to help you.

Contact seller

There are 2 kinds of digital purchases: 

  • Instant downloads: Ready-made files that are available once your payment is confirmed. If you paid with PayPal or a credit card on Etsy, it may take a few minutes for your download link to be sent to you. 
  • Made-to-order downloads: Digital items that the seller will make to your specifications after you purchase them. The seller will send your files to you once they have completed them. 

When your digital files are available for download, you will receive an email. Select View your files on Etsy to be taken to the Purchases section of your Etsy account to download files.

You can't download a digital purchase through the Etsy app at this time. To download a digital file, please sign in to Etsy on your mobile browser or computer.

I can’t find my download notification email

First, check your spam or junk inbox. If you use Gmail, also check your Social and Promotions tabs. If it’s not there, adding transaction@account.etsy.com or noreply@etsy.com to your address book or safe list can help you locate these emails in the future.

For now, you can still access your digital purchases in your account.

Where can I find my digital purchases in my account?

To access your digital files from your account:

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and go to Your account.
  2. Go to Purchases.
  3. Next to the order, select Download Files. This goes to the Downloads page for all the files attached to your order.

You can also select View Receipt at the top of an item’s listing page to go to Purchases, where you can download the item.

There are generally no limits for when or how many times you can download a file. In most cases, you can access a file any time on your Purchases page, provided the transaction hasn't been canceled or removed.

If your payment is still processing, the Download Files button will be gray.

When will I receive my made-to-order digital item? 

The delivery window for made-to-order digital items depends on the seller. Please coordinate with the seller through Messages to establish the completion time for your order. 

To see the status of your made-to-order digital item, go to the Purchases  section of your Etsy account. Items that the seller is still working on are shown as In progress. 

Once the seller finishes your order, you will receive an email with a link to download your digital file. You can also access your files by going to Purchases and selecting the Download files button. You will be able to leave a review for your purchase after you download your file.

I purchased a digital item, but I don't have an Etsy account

If you purchased an instant digital download as a guest, you'll find a link to download your files in the receipt email that was sent to you after the purchase. 

Made-to-order digital items will be sent once the seller has finished them. If you no longer have access to the email account you used to make the original purchase, please contact the seller directly to discuss how they can send you your files.

I’m having trouble downloading my files

If nothing happens when you click the download links, it’s possible that there’s an issue with your web browser. Please disable any non-standard add-ons like ad blockers or toolbars that you’ve installed and try again.

If your computer states that the file has been corrupted, delete the file and try downloading it again. If you still can't open the file, please contact the seller through Etsy Messages for further assistance.

The type of file you’ll be downloading is shown under the Highlights section of a digital listing. If your computer is unable to open the file, it’s possible that you’re missing the program required to open the file type. 

If you continue to have trouble, contact Etsy Support.

My download is a ZIP file

Some digital items are delivered as a ZIP file, which bundles one or more files into a single download. Before you can use the files inside, you'll need to unzip (or extract) the folder.

To unzip a ZIP file: 

  • On a computer: Double-click the ZIP file or right-click it and select Extract.
  • On a phone or tablet: You may need to use your device's file manager or a compatible app to unzip the file. It’s not possible to download any digital items through the Etsy app at this time.

If you're unable to open the files after unzipping them, you may need software that's compatible with that file type. Check the listing’s description to see if there’s file type information, any software requirements, or instructions provided by the seller. If you're still unable to open the files, contact the seller for help.

I want a refund or want to cancel my digital item

On the item page for a digital listing, you will see that digital listings are not able to be returned or canceled.

If there’s a problem with your digital order, like it’s not as described in the listing or the seller never delivers the file, you may be covered under Etsy’s Purchase Protection. 

 Learn how to get help with your order.

results.name: How VAT Works on Digital Items
results.title: How VAT Works on Digital Items
results.body:
Etsy collects and remits VAT on digital items purchased by buyers located in certain countries.

VAT stands for value-added tax. It's a tax based on the consumption of goods and services that are commonly found in the EU and select other regions of the world.

VAT is also known as JCT, GST, HST, SST, PST, RST or QST in some countries and regions.

VAT may be charged to buyers on their purchases (“VAT on Items Sold on Etsy”) as well as to eligible sellers on their paid seller fees ("VAT on seller fees”).

The information below is for VAT rules on the sale of digital items delivered via automatic download to buyers in:

  • Armenia
  • Australia
  • Bosnia
  • Canada
  • Chile
  • Colombia
  • Egypt
  • the EU
  • Georgia (country)
  • Ghana
  • Kazakhstan
  • Kyrgyzstan
  • Iceland
  • India
  • Indonesia
  • Kenya
  • Malaysia
  • Mexico
  • Moldova
  • Morocco
  • New Zealand
  • Nigeria
  • Norway
  • Peru
  • Phillippines
  • Saudi Arabia
  • Serbia
  • Singapore
  • South Africa
  • South Korea
  • Switzerland
  • Taiwan
  • Tanzania
  • Thailand
  • Türkiye
  • Uganda
  • Ukraine
  • the United Arab Emirates
  • the United Kingdom
  • Uzbekistan
  • Vietnam

This does not apply to physical goods. Learn how VAT works on physical items.

Etsy and digital VAT

Buyers—not Etsy or Etsy sellers—pay VAT as part of their total purchase price when buying digital items.

If you sell digital items, no matter where your shop is located, buyers located in countries on the list above will be charged VAT.

If you sell digital items to buyers in Canada, learn when your buyers will be charged Canadian taxes.

Some examples of digital items:

  • E-books 
  • Digital patterns 
  • Downloadable PDFs

In all cases, Etsy will take the VAT paid by the buyer and remit to the relevant tax authorities. Sellers are not responsible for adding VAT to their digital listing prices. If you have any questions regarding your tax liability on digital items that you sell, please contact your tax advisor.

How digital VAT works for buyers

Etsy automatically detects if the buyer is in one of these countries and adds the appropriate VAT to the listing price if the item is a digital file download.

Buyers see the total price with VAT included on each listing that applies, as well as in their cart, invoice, and purchase page.

Buyers will pay the listing price and VAT for digital items purchased from any seller.

Digital VAT and your Payment account

Etsy Payments

For transactions where Etsy Payments is the payment method, Etsy will automatically collect VAT from the buyer. The VAT will be deducted from the order before the funds are placed in the seller’s Payment account.

Standalone PayPal 

For transactions made with the seller's stand-alone PayPal account, the VAT costs are added to the seller’s Payment account.

Remember, Etsy can't directly collect the VAT charged to buyers when they make a payment to the seller's own PayPal account. If a seller accepts payment in their own PayPal account, applicable VAT will be added to the seller’s Payment account once the buyer completes checkout. This way, Etsy can then remit it.

results.name: How Printed Items From Digital Purchases Work for Sellers
results.title: How Printed Items From Digital Purchases Work for Sellers
results.body:
Etsy is testing a new way for buyers to turn eligible digital files they purchase on Etsy’s website into printed items. If you have eligible digital listings, they may be included in this test automatically. You can opt out if you don’t want your eligible listings to be included.

How does the printed item experience work?

After purchasing an eligible digital file, buyers may see an option to order it as a printed item through a separate checkout on Etsy. Buyers can choose from available options, select the digital file they want to use, preview the item, and place a separate order.

Ventur Editions, a third party print provider, sells and fulfills the printed item from their shop:

  • The printed item has its own listing and reviews.
  • If there’s an issue with the order, Ventur Editions provides support.

Are my listings eligible?

Your digital listings may be included in the test if: 

  • Your shop based in the US or Canada
  • You don't already offer a physical version of the design or use your own print-on-demand integration
  • The file meets the print partner’s requirements for high-quality printing

Can I opt out?

If you don’t want your eligible digital listings included in the test, you can opt out. Once you opt out, the option to order printed items will no longer appear after purchases of your eligible listings. For this test, the opt-out applies to your shop rather than individual listings.

Opting out removes print options from being surfaced after purchases of your eligible listings. It doesn’t prevent buyers from independently accessing Ventur Editions’ services with the content they’ve downloaded. 

To opt out:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Select Options.
  4. Go to Allow buyers to purchase digital prints and select Disabled.

results.name: How to Manage Your Digital Listings
results.title: How to Manage Your Digital Listings
results.body:
Digital items come in two categories: 

  • Instant downloads: Ready-made files that the buyer can access immediately upon purchase
  • Made-to-order downloads: Custom files made to a buyer’s specification that will be sent to them upon completion.

Like handmade items, digital items listed in your store must be made and/or designed by you, the seller.

Follow the instructions to list an item on Etsy and choose Digital files under the What type of item is it? prompt. To create a made-to-order digital listing: 

  1. Go to the When did you make it? dropdown.
  2. Select Made To Order.

How to add files to your digital listing

When listing a digital item that is an instant download, you’ll need to upload the files that the buyer is purchasing when you create the listing. You can upload up to five digital files. The maximum size for each file is 20MB.

  • .bmp
  • .doc
  • .gif
  • .jpeg
  • .jpg
  • .mobi
  • .mov
  • .mp3
  • .mpeg
  • .pdf
  • .png
  • .psp
  • .rtf
  • .stl
  • .txt
  • .zip
  • .ePUB
  • .iBook

Uploaded files will appear in a list with their names, file sizes, and upload dates. The file names you see will be the same ones your buyers see. We don't have a way of editing the name after uploading, so be sure to name your files appropriately first.

File names are limited to 70 alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, or hyphens.

Add a note for buyers

You can add a note for buyers that will apply to all digital listings purchased from your shop. After a purchase, a buyer can see the note on their Downloads page.

Can I offer variations for my digital items?

No, you can’t offer variations for digital items.

How can I change the file attached to an instant digital listing?

To remove a file, select the X icon next to its file name when you create or edit a listing, and add new files to the listing using the Add files button. You will be unable to publish or save an instant digital listing if there is no file attached to it. Canceling an order is the only way to revoke a buyer’s access to a file after it has been purchased. 

If I exclusively sell digital items, will I be eligible for Star Seller?

Yes, if you sell only digital items, you’re still eligible for Star Seller. When you view your Star Seller dashboard you won’t see an on-time shipping & tracking score, but you’ll still be considered based on other metrics.

How to complete made-to-order digital orders

Unlike instant downloads, you don’t upload a file when creating a made-to-order digital listing. Once you’re ready to send the finished file to the buyer, complete the order through the following steps:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager and select Orders. 
  2. Your incomplete orders are displayed under the New tab. 
  3. Check the box of the order you want to finish, then choose Complete order. 
  4. Select the Upload file button. You can attach up to five files with a maximum size of 20MB each.
  5. Finish by selecting the Complete order button. The buyer will be notified by email that their order is now available for download.

results.name: When Can I Leave a Review for My Order?
results.title: When Can I Leave a Review for My Order?
results.body:
You can leave a review after the date your order is estimated to be delivered. You’ll see Leave a review or report an issue on [date] with the order on your Purchases page.

How long do I have to leave a review? 

From your estimated delivery date, you have 100 days to leave a review and 30 days to open a case.

How can I leave a review if I purchased an item as a guest? 

If you purchased as a guest, you’ll need to connect your order to an Etsy account before leaving a review or opening a case.  

When can I leave a review for a digital item? 

If you purchased a digital item, you can leave a review once you download the file.

results.name: How to Offer Custom Items
results.title: How to Offer Custom Items
results.body:
Enabling custom order requests shows buyers that you can work with them to create  one-of-a-kind items beyond what you have available in your inventory. If a shopper requests a custom item, you can convert their request to a custom listing. 

How to enable custom order requests

You'll be able to add custom order requests once your shop is open to the public. Custom order requests can only be enabled on Etsy.com.

To enable custom order requests:

  1. Go to Shop Manager.
  2. Go to Settings.
  3. Go to Options.
  4. Under Custom order requests, select Enabled.
  5. Select Save.

A Request Custom Order button will appear on your shop homepage. 

The maximum processing time you can place on a custom order is 6-8 weeks.

What your buyer will see

When a buyer chooses Request Custom Order, they'll be able to send you a message describing what they're looking for and the date they need it by (if there is a deadline).

If you need more information, send your buyer a message to work out the details.

How you and your buyer complete a custom order

When the buyer initially requests an item, you'll receive a message. If it’s a new message, it will be in your Custom Requests folder. If it’s part of an existing message thread, it will be in your Inbox. 

Once you work out the details of exactly what the buyer wants and how much it will cost, create a custom, private listing directly from the original Custom Request Message thread.

It's not possible to choose a calculated shipping profile for custom orders at this time.

Additional information about custom listings

  • The listing won't appear in your public shop or in search, which means that other buyers won't be able to purchase it. Once your listing is sold, though, it will appear on your public Sold Items page with your other sold listings.  
  • Your private custom listings are viewable from your Listings page. They’ll be labeled Private. 
  • Once you publish this listing, we'll send your buyer an email with a button to purchase the listing. 
  • Private listings cannot be created for digital items. If you want to offer a custom digital item, consider setting up made-to-order digital listings in your shop.
  • If your buyer sent the request through a regular message, you can still create a private custom listing. In the message, select Create custom order. Fill out the required information, then choose Send private listing.

How custom listings differ from listing variations

Listing variations offer an item you already make, with different options a buyer can choose from, such as color, size, styles, or materials. These options are available for any buyer who visits your website to purchase. 

Listings created from a custom request are private between you and the buyer. When a custom listing is created, that item is only available for the buyer who made the request and won’t be displayed on your storefront. 

Learn more about using and managing custom orders.

Questions about listings?

Ask the Community

results.name: How to Order a Printed Item From a Digital File on Etsy
results.title: How to Order a Printed Item From a Digital File on Etsy
results.body:
After purchasing select digital files on Etsy.com, you may have the option to order them as printed items. You’ll place a new order from Ventur Editions, a third party print provider.

How do I order a printed item?

To order a printed item of an eligible digital file:

  1. If a digital file is eligible, you can choose View print options on post-purchase pages such as the digital file’s order confirmation.
  2. On the print listing, select Add file. You can choose to Use last purchase, select from Etsy purchases, or Upload from your computer. 
  3. Choose from the available size and customization options. Available choices will depend on your digital file and the item you select.
  4. Preview your item and make sure it looks the way you want. Your image may be cropped slightly to fit the selected item.
  5. Confirm your selections are correct.
  6. Select Buy it now or Add to cart and begin the checkout process.

What kinds of prints can I order?

Print options may include: 

  • Indoor wall tapestries
  • Framed posters
  • Matte canvases
  • Metal art signs
  • Rolled posters
  • Coffee mugs
  • Canvas tote bags
  • Greeting cards 
  • Crewneck sweatshirt

Who makes and fulfills my order?

Your printed item is a new order from Ventur Editions, separate from the digital file you purchased from an Etsy seller.

  • Ventur Editions prints and fulfills your order. Ventur Editions is the seller and you will be checking out from their shop. 
  • If you want to share feedback about the printed item after it arrives, make sure you review the Ventur Editions order.
  • If you have questions or need help with your order, contact Ventur Editions through your printed item order in Purchases and reviews.

results.name: How to Add or Edit Your Post-Purchase Message to Buyers
results.title: How to Add or Edit Your Post-Purchase Message to Buyers
results.body:
Message to Buyers is a short note you can include in the receipt page and order confirmation email that your buyers receive after purchasing from your shop.

Consider using your message to thank your customer for their purchase, inform them about standard shipping practices, or provide any other information you think they may need to know.

To add or edit your Message to Buyers on Etsy.com: 

  1. Sign in and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Go to Settings.
  3. Select Info & Appearance. 
  4. Go to Message to Buyers and enter your message.
  5. Select Save Changes.

If you sell digital items, include a Message to Buyers for Digital Items. This message is included on the Downloads page for digital orders. It applies to all digital listings purchased from your shop. 

You can also send other messages to buyers about their order. Learn more about Messages.

results.name: EU Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive (ECGT)
results.title: EU Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive (ECGT)
results.body:
The EU Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive (ECGT), which takes effect on September 27, 2026, updates EU consumer protection laws to address environmental claims and introduces new information requirements around consumer guarantee rights and product durability and repairability. 

This article is intended as a practical guide based on our interpretation of ECGT and is not legal advice. Sellers should review their obligations under ECGT and consider consulting a legal professional to fully understand how the regulation applies to them. Sellers remain responsible for the accuracy and compliance of their listings.

In this article:

  • Who ECGT applies to
  • Legal guarantee for physical items
  • Legal guarantee for digital items
  • Additional buyer information
  • Environmental claims

Who ECGT applies to

ECGT applies to you if: 

  • You market items to buyers in the European Economic Area (EEA), which includes all EU member states, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway. 

and

  • You meet the definition of a “trader”, which may include businesses or professional sellers. Whether you’re considered a trader under EU regulation is complex and we always recommend reaching out to a legal advisor for information tailored to your business. 

If you signed up on Etsy as a “business” seller, you’re automatically designated as a “trader” within your shop and listings. You can update your “trader” status in your Policy Setting at any time. You are responsible for keeping this information accurate. 

Legal guarantee for physical items

Under ECGT, traders are required to remind EEA buyers of the two-year statutory warranty that applies to physical goods they purchase, using the set format of the EU harmonised notice. This warranty gives buyers the right to a repair, replacement, or refund if an item doesn’t conform to its description, within two years of delivery. 

If you are a trader, the EU harmonised notice will automatically surface, in the applicable language, on applicable listings of items marketed towards EEA buyers. You’ll be notified as part of the listing creation process when this notice will surface on your listing. If you have questions about how this notice appears on your listings, contact Etsy Support. 

Legal guarantee for digital items

If you are a trader that sells digital items (such as downloadable files) to EEA buyers, a separate legal guarantee of conformity may apply under EU law. This guarantee gives buyers the right to a fix or refund if a digital item doesn't conform to its description.

If you are a trader, the legal guarantee notice will automatically surface, in the applicable language, on applicable digital listings for EEA buyers. The following text will be displayed: "This product comes with a legal guarantee of conformity under EU laws." You’ll be notified as part of the listing process when this notice will surface on your listing. 

Additional buyer information

Depending on your item and what you offer, you may need to provide additional warranty, service, or repair details, if applicable to your listing. 

These fields include: 

  • Commercial warranty or guarantee terms: If you offer a commercial warranty or guarantee beyond the statutory legal guarantee described above, you should include its details. 
  • GARAN label: You should determine whether your commercial warranty qualifies for the EU’s harmonized GARAN label for commercial guarantees of durability – generally, this depends on whether your warranty lasts more than two years, is provided at no additional cost, and covers the entire product. If your warranty qualifies, provide the duration of your warranty, your brand name and the product’s model identifier to surface a GARAN label as part of your listing. You are responsible for the accuracy of any information you input for the GARAN label. 
  • Repair, after-sales support, delivery, and software update information: If applicable to your item, you should provide details about any after-sales services and repairability, including a repairability score where required, availability of spare parts, environmentally friendly delivery options, or the duration of free software updates. 

Environmental claims

Under ECGT, environmental claims must be specific and backed by evidence. The following types of claims are generally prohibited in listings marketing items to buyers in the EEA: 

  • Generic terms like “eco-friendly,” “green,” or “sustainable” unless backed by recognized excellent environmental performance. 
  • Claims based on offsets of greenhouse gas emissions like “carbon neutral” and “net zero”. 
  • Claims about your entire shop or businesses that only relate to certain items or listings. 

When making a claim, consider: 

  • Specificity: Describe the specific material or characteristic your claim is based on – for example, “100% recycled cotton” or “made from 50% post-consumer recycled polyester”. 
  • Material and material feature attributes: Etsy’s listing attributes include Materials (such as Organic Cotton, Recycled Glass, or Hemp) and Material Features (such as Upcycled, Plastic-Free, Reusable, or Vegan). By selecting one of these attributes, you are certifying that your item meets that attribute’s description and that you have the necessary supporting documentation. Learn more about attributes.
  • Certifications: If you reference a certification or sustainability label (such as GOTS or RCS) in your listing description, make sure it’s current, is based on an ECGT-compliant certification scheme, covers your specific item, and that you have the necessary authorization to reference it. 
  • Record-keeping: Keep records that support any claims you make, such as technical evidence, bills of materials, supplier declarations, product labels, or certification documents. 

If you have concerns about a claim on a listing, you can contact Etsy Support. More broadly, Etsy may remove or restrict listings that it becomes aware of that do not comply with the requirements under ECGT.

results.name: Purchasing Etsy Items Through ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Copilot
results.title: Purchasing Etsy Items Through ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Copilot
results.body:
Etsy has partnered with OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft to allow some Etsy listings to be purchased directly in ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Copilot. 

You must be logged into a ChatGPT, Google, or Microsoft account in order to use these features. After checking out, you’ll receive an email from Etsy confirming your order. You can access your order history in ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, or Copilot, as well as on Etsy if you connect your order to an Etsy account with the email address used for your purchase. 

At this time, only shoppers in the United States can purchase Etsy items through ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Copilot.

What payment methods can I use when checking out on ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Copilot? 

When checking out, you can pay by: 

  • Credit or debit card
  • Bank account via Link
  • Apple Pay
  • Google Pay 

Transactions can be completed in United States dollars (USD) only. 

At this time, Etsy gift cards and coupons cannot be used for orders placed through ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Copilot.

How do I connect my order to an Etsy account? 

When you make a purchase through ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, or Copilot, you will check out as a guest with Etsy. Your order will not automatically be connected to your Etsy account.

Connect your Etsy account in order to:

  • Leave a review
  • Message the seller
  • Send a Help with Order request
  • File a Support ticket  

To link your order to an existing Etsy account:

  1. Open your order confirmation email from your purchase.
  2. Select View Order in the email.
  3. Sign into Etsy using the email address used for your purchase.

If you do not already have an Etsy account, you’ll need to create one. Learn how to connect a guest order to an Etsy account. 

How do I download a digital item purchased through ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, or Copilot? 

A link to download your digital files is located in the receipt email sent to you after your purchase. Learn more about downloading a digital item. 

How do I get help with my order? 

If you have questions about your order, such as order status, shipping address updates, and cancellations, contact the seller through Etsy. Learn more about getting help with your order on Etsy. 

If you have issues prior to purchasing or notice unauthorized orders:

  • In your ChatGPT account: contact OpenAI
  • In your Gemini or Google AI Mode account: contact Google
  • In your Copilot account: contact Microsoft

results.name: What Can I Sell on Etsy?
results.title: What Can I Sell on Etsy?
results.body:
The Etsy marketplace connects people looking for unique goods with independent sellers around the world. Everything listed for sale on Etsy must either be made, designed, handpicked or sourced by you. All items sold on Etsy must also follow our Prohibited Items Policy.

It is your responsibility to make sure your shop and its items are in compliance with Etsy's policies. The images you use in your listings must also comply with our Listing Image Requirements. Before buying or selling on Etsy, please review our Terms of Use.

Reselling mass-produced items is not allowed on Etsy. We allow limited exceptions for creative items that are handpicked or sourced by sellers. Learn more about what is allowed.

Learn more about Etsy’s Creativity Standards.

Jump to a section:

  • Made by a seller
  • Designed by a seller
  • Handpicked by a seller
  • Sourced by a seller
  • Prohibited items
  • AI-generated content
  • Listings that violate Etsy's Intellectual Property Policy
  • Services or rentals
  • Metaphysical services or items
  • What happens if I find a listing that violates Etsy's policies?

Made by a seller

Items that fall under "Made by a seller" are physical items that are made by you, the seller.

Any items made by you, the seller, must:

  • Be physically made by hand, or produced using computerized tools like a 3D printer, CNC or Cricut machine
  • Only include handcrafted items, hand altered items, hand assembled items or items produced using computerized tools
  • Use your own photographs in your listings

Read Etsy’s Creativity Standards.

Can I resell handmade items?

Reselling is not allowed in the Handmade category on Etsy. Reselling on Etsy means listing an item as handmade when you, the seller, weren’t involved in designing or making that item. Learn more about reselling on Etsy. 

Designed by a seller

As a seller, you can offer your original design as a digital download, or use a third party to produce or print your design onto a physical item. This category also includes seller-prompted AI creations. 

Digital items listed in your store must be made and/or designed by you, the seller. Digital items can either be premade files, or files you custom make and deliver to the buyer after purchase. 

Learn more about how to manage digital listings. 

Seller-prompted AI creations must disclose the use of AI. 

If you work with a production partner, you must disclose that production partner in your relevant listings.

Handpicked by a seller

Items that fall under "Handpicked by a seller" include vintage items that are at least 20 years old, items from nature, and certain collections of items that a seller selected and curated for sale.

Learn more about selling items curated by you in Etsy’s Creativity Standards.

Sourced by a seller

Items that fall under "Sourced by a seller" enable buyer creativity, like craft supplies, party decorations and items personalized with a buyer's unique text or image.

Learn more about what can be sold in this category in Etsy’s Creativity Standards.

Prohibited items

Several types of items are prohibited from being sold on Etsy, including:

  • Alcohol, tobacco, drugs, drug paraphernalia, and medical drugs
  • Certain animal products and human remains
  • Dangerous items, including hazardous materials, recalled items, and weapons
  • Hate items, including items that promote, support, or glorify hatred
  • Illegal items, items promoting illegal activity, and highly regulated items
  • Internationally regulated items
  • Pornography and mature content
  • Violent items, including items that promote, support, or glorify violence

Learn more about prohibited items.

AI-generated content

Etsy allows sellers to use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to create certain items, as long as they contribute their own creative input and follow Etsy’s policies. Sellers must disclose within their listing description if an item is created with the use of AI.

Sellers are allowed to use their original prompts in combination with AI tools to create the products they sell on Etsy. Permitted examples might include a fantasy scene based on a seller’s original prompt and produced by an AI generator, or a custom portrait of a buyer’s pet generated using AI tools. 

Some forms of AI-generated content are not allowed on Etsy, including:

  • Bot-generated content
  • AI-generated functional instructions, such as craft patterns, recipes, and instructions
  • AI prompt bundles

Learn more about Etsy’s stance on AI creations.

Listings that violate Etsy's Intellectual Property Policy

As a venue, Etsy isn’t in a position to offer legal advice or determine whether your shop content infringes someone else’s intellectual property. 

If you're not sure if your item(s) infringe someone’s intellectual property, you can contact the intellectual property owner or consult an attorney. 

If Etsy receives proper notice of intellectual property infringement, we will comply with our policy and remove the specified material.

Services or rentals

In general, services, including rentals, are not allowed to be sold on Etsy. Only services that produce a new tangible item that meets our Seller Policies may be sold on Etsy. 

Learn more about the services that may qualify to be sold on Etsy.

Metaphysical services or items

Metaphysical services, such as reiki and spell casting, are prohibited on Etsy. With this in mind, tarot or psychic readings that include a physical or digital copy of said readings (e.g., a recording, email, or tarot spread photo) may be sold on Etsy. 

Supplies related to spell work, such as herbs, crystals, candles, and tinctures, may be sold on Etsy as long as they are not listed with metaphysical claims. 

What happens if I find a listing that violates Etsy’s policies?

You can report a listing that appears to violate our policies. Etsy may review and/or remove any listings that violate our policies.

results.name: Will I Have to Pay for Tax, Customs, or Tariffs on My Order?
results.title: Will I Have to Pay for Tax, Customs, or Tariffs on My Order?
results.body:
When buying from another country, you may be charged additional fees depending on the import taxes and/or customs duties of your home country. You may need to pay the charges once you receive your order, or Etsy may be required to collect the tax at checkout to send to the tax authorities.

When buying from a seller in your country, you may be charged sales tax or VAT depending on your country’s requirements for online purchases. Purchases for which Etsy is required to charge sales tax at checkout differ between states and countries.

Jump to a section:

  • Am I responsible for paying customs fees?
  • When does Etsy collect and remit US sales tax?
  • When does Etsy collect and remit VAT-type taxes?
  • How does VAT work for digital purchases?
  • How do I download my VAT invoice?

Am I responsible for paying customs fees?

Customs fees are placed on physical goods that are imported into a country from another country or territory. These fees are applied to international sales, but never domestic.

As a buyer, you are generally responsible for paying the additional costs such as duties, taxes, tariffs, and customs clearance fees. In some countries, Etsy is obligated to collect taxes such as VAT on imported goods, which are then sent to tax authorities. 

Most customs charges are due once the package arrives in the destination country. The cost of the charges is based on: 

  • The price and type of item 
  • The package weight and dimensions 
  • The origin country the package is being shipped from 
  • The taxes, duties, and fees of the destination country

If you buy a package from a seller located in a different country, a notice is displayed at checkout saying that additional fees and duties may apply. However this notice does not mean that additional charges for your order are guaranteed. Your local customs office can be contacted to see if additional charges need to be paid for your order.

If you only want to shop within your own country, use search filters to find local sellers on Etsy.

If you're in the US, you're not responsible for unexpected customs fees on orders shipped from other countries. Sellers are required to use Delivery Duty Paid (DDP) shipping when sending orders to the US, which means duties and import fees must be paid upfront. If you're charged unexpected customs fees, reach out to the seller for help. If the seller is unable to help you, open a case.

When does Etsy collect and remit US sales tax?

As of August 29, 2025, most packages shipped to the US will be subject to tariffs. Tariffs are taxes applied by a country's government on imported goods. How these tariffs are paid depends on the shipping method the seller uses.

Delivered Duty Paid (DDP): The seller pays the tariffs up front, and the cost is included in the total at checkout. This ensures a smoother delivery process with no surprise fees at the time of delivery.

Delivered Duty Unpaid (DDU): The buyer is responsible for paying any tariffs and associated fees directly to the shipping carrier upon delivery.

We are encouraging sellers to ship with Delivery Duty Paid (DDP). Since sellers have different shipping processes, the best way to know if your order includes tariffs is to contact the seller directly through Messages. They will be able to confirm the shipping method used and answer questions about your order. 

Etsy is legally required to charge sales tax if the US state you’re in mandates it. The price you see on Etsy for an item sold by a US seller is the price you pay, so you should not be charged any additional taxes on delivery.

Check if your US state collects sales tax or delivery fees on online purchases.

If you purchase something for a US tax-exempt organization, learn how to submit a tax-exemption form to Etsy.

When does Etsy collect and remit VAT-type taxes?

VAT, or value-added tax, is sales tax based on the purchase of goods and services that are commonly found in the EU and select other regions of the world.

Sales taxes have many names. For example, it is known as VAT in Europe; JCT in Japan; GST in New Zealand, Australia, and India; and GST/HST in Canada.

Additional duties and taxes may be charged to buyers when physical goods are delivered cross-border between countries or states. 

Australia requires Etsy to collect and remit GST on applicable goods sold to Australian buyers on orders that meet the following criteria: 

  • Less than or equal to $1,000 AUD

For amounts higher than $1,000 AUD, GST and any other taxes are charged and collected at the border rather than by Etsy. 

Etsy doesn’t collect GST for goods purchased from and delivered to locations in Australia. Since Etsy requires sellers to list their prices inclusive of GST, you shouldn’t have to pay any additional amounts other than the total price displayed at checkout.

Etsy is required to collect GST/HST as well as PST in Saskatchewan and British Columbia, RST in Manitoba, and QST in Quebec. Etsy automatically includes tax in the total you see at checkout. To learn more about these tax requirements you can visit Canada’s government website for more information. 

  • Seller added GST/HST ID: If an item is being shipped from a seller in Canada to a buyer in Canada, the listing price automatically includes GST/HST. 
  • Seller did not add GST/HST ID: GST/HST is charged during checkout when a physical item will ship from a Canadian seller to a buyer in Canada, or if it is a digital item that is sold to a Canadian buyer from a Canadian seller. 
  • Seller added QST ID: If an item is shipped from a Canadian seller to a Quebec buyer, the listing price automatically includes QST. 
  • Seller did not add QST ID: QST is charged at checkout when a physical item is sold from a Canadian address to a buyer located in Quebec, or a digital item is sold to a buyer in Quebec, from sellers in other provinces or outside Canada. 
  • British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST): PST is charged at checkout on all physical and digital downloads that are delivered to buyers located in British Columbia 
  • Saskatchewan Provincial Sales Tax (PST): PST is charged at checkout on all physical items and certain digital downloads that are delivered to buyers in Saskatchewan. 
  • Manitoba Retails Sales Tax (RST): RST is charged at checkout on physical items and certain digital downloads that are delivered to buyers in Manitoba. 

For goods sold within the European Union, VAT—if applicable —is included in the purchase price at the time of sale. Since Etsy requires sellers to list their prices inclusive of VAT, you shouldn’t have to pay any additional amounts other than the total price displayed at checkout.

As of July 1 2026, both VAT and customs duties apply to all goods being shipped from outside the EU into the EU.

For purchases with a value less than €150, Etsy charges VAT at checkout. A customs duty of €3 per item also applies to these purchases. Depending on how the seller ships the item, this fee may be included in the amount paid at checkout or collected upon delivery.

For purchases with a value exceeding €150 (excluding shipping and gift wrap), you may be charged VAT and customs duties upon delivery unless the seller ships the item with duties paid in advance.

New Zealand requires Etsy to collect and remit GST on applicable goods sold to New Zealand buyers from overseas that meet the following criteria:

  • The buyer is located in New Zealand (based on delivery address).
  • The seller is not located in New Zealand.

Etsy doesn’t collect GST where the goods are located in New Zealand. Since Etsy requires sellers to list their prices inclusive of GST, you shouldn’t have to pay any additional amounts other than the total price displayed at checkout.

Norway requires Etsy to collect and remit VAT on applicable goods sold to Norway buyers from overseas that meet the following criteria:

  • The seller is located outside Norway.
  • The delivery address is in Norway.
  • The package has items less than 3,000 NOK.
  • The item is subject to VAT at the standard rate.

Etsy does not charge VAT on goods subject to excise duty, such as food and drink. These taxes will be collected at the border.

For amounts higher than 3,000 NOK, and other orders that don’t meet the above criteria, VAT is charged and collected at the border.

Etsy doesn’t collect VAT where the goods are on transactions between buyers and sellers both located in Norway. Since Etsy requires sellers to list their prices inclusive of VAT, you shouldn’t have to pay any additional amounts other than the total price displayed at checkout.

Sellers must pass Etsy's VOEC number to their postal/carrier service electronically. If your seller doesn’t do this, then you may be charged VAT a second time upon delivery of the item.

Singapore requires Etsy to collect and remit GST on applicable goods from buyers on orders that meet the following criteria:

  • The purchase is for a physical item
  • The recipient is located in Singapore
  • The total value of the item (including gift wrap but excluding delivery) is less than $400 SGD.
  • The goods are shipped from outside Singapore

GST is applied to the full order total, which includes item price and shipping

For items with a value $400 SGD and more, GST is charged and collected at the border.

Etsy doesn’t collect GST where the goods are located in Singapore and the transaction is between buyers and sellers both located in Singapore. Etsy requires sellers in Singapore to list their physical item prices inclusive of GST. If you’re located in Singapore and are buying a physical item from a Singapore seller, you shouldn’t have to pay any additional amount past the total price displayed at checkout.

The UK requires Etsy to collect and remit VAT on applicable goods from buyers on orders that meet the following criteria:

  • The purchase is for a physical item. 
  • The recipient is located in the UK.
  • The total value of the package (including gift wrap but excluding delivery) is less than or equal to £135 GBP.
  • VAT is applied to the full order total, which includes item price, delivery, and gift wrap charges.
  • The goods are shipped from outside the UK.*

*Etsy isn't obligated to collect VAT on packages from the EU to Northern Ireland, or on packages from Northern Ireland to other parts of the UK.

For amounts higher than £135 GBP, VAT is charged and collected at the border.

Etsy doesn’t collect VAT where the goods are located in the UK and the transaction is between buyers and sellers both located in the UK. Since Etsy requires sellers to list their prices inclusive of VAT, you shouldn’t have to pay any additional amounts other than the total price displayed at checkout. 

If you’re in a country where Etsy collects VAT or similar taxes, your basket details will show the item price, postage costs, and any additional add-ons such as gift wrap at checkout.

For questions about the item’s prices and the inclusion of VAT, it’s best that you contact the seller directly.

If you believe the incorrect VAT rate was charged, please reach out to us.

How does VAT work for digital purchase? 

If Etsy is required to collect the VAT or similar taxes, Etsy automatically collects and adds the appropriate amount to the listing price when you purchase a downloadable digital item.

Some examples of digital items:

  • E-books 
  • Digital patterns 
  • Downloadable PDFs

You can see the total price with VAT or similar tax included on each listing that applies, as well as in your basket, invoice, and purchase page.

All digital downloads on Etsy are considered B2C (business to consumer) purchases and therefore you aren’t required to provide a VAT ID (or similar tax ID). 

How do I download my VAT invoice?

For physical items imported to Australia and New Zealand, you can download an official GST invoice. If you're located in the EU and the United Kingdom, you can see the VAT charges on your purchase receipt.

Outside this, it's the seller's responsibility to provide a legally-compliant VAT invoice when required. The default receipt from Etsy can't be used for this purpose. 

If you need a tax invoice for your purchase, you’ll need to contact the seller directly before placing the order to make sure they can facilitate your request. 

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and go to Your account.
  2. Go to Purchases and reviews.
  3. Select the View receipt next to your item. 
  4. If you’re in the UK or EU, select Print Options to download your invoice. For all other locations, select View official invoice. 

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and go to Your account.
  2. Go to Purchases and reviews.
  3. Select the View receipt next to your item. 
  4. Select View official invoice to see the invoice. 

We do not provide VAT invoices for gift cards purchased on Etsy

VAT invoices for buyers in Taiwan

If you’re located in Taiwan, we are partnering with Taxamo who will send the VAT invoice to the email address associated with your purchase. Learn more about VAT invoices in Taiwan.

results.name: How to Set Up Your Shop Policies
results.title: How to Set Up Your Shop Policies
results.body:
To set up your shop policies:

  1. On Etsy.com, open Shop Manager.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Choose Policy Settings.

Your policies have several sections and are separated into different tabs: Returns & exchanges; Cancellations; Privacy, and Fixed. 

Policies can’t be added or edited from the Etsy Seller app. Please use the mobile web or desktop versions of Etsy to update your policies.

Choose a section to learn more:
  • Returns & exchanges
  • Cancellations
  • Privacy
  • Fixed Policies 

Returns & exchanges

From this tab, you can create and edit the various return and exchange policies that you use when selling non-digital items on Etsy. These policies are applied as you see fit to your individual listings rather than being a blanket return policy for your entire shop. 

If you’re a seller outside of the EU, you must set a return policy whenever you edit or create a new listing for a physical item, even if it is to let buyers know you do not accept returns or exchanges on that listing. 

Learn how to set return policies on your listings.

EU right of withdrawal

Regulations in the EU give buyers the right to cancel or return their orders within 14 days of delivery. If you set your return policy to less than 14 days, a banner reminding you of the EU right of withdrawal will appear on your Returns and exchanges policy page.

Read more about how EU regulations may affect your shop.

If you are a “trader” that sells to EU/EEA states, there may be additional information that needs to be added to your individual listings under General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) requirements.

Learn more about how to prepare your shop to meet GPSR requirements.

If you signed up on Etsy as a “business” seller, meaning you’ve registered your business with a government agency and have a business ID number or are an incorporated business on Etsy, and you ship to buyers in the EU and/or EEA, we’ve automatically added “trader” status to your listings. 

The EU Omnibus Directive is a consumer protection directive that has passed in the European Union and may impact your shop. This directive requires business sellers who ship to the EU and/or EEA to identify themselves to buyers as “traders.”

The definition of a “trader” under the directive may vary depending on which countries in the EU and/or EEA you ship to. If you’re unsure if you would be recognized as a trader, we recommend that you reach out to a legal advisor. 

You can change your “trader” status in your policy settings at any time by selecting Edit in the Seller details section of your public shop. Choose your shop under Sales Channels in Shop Manager. 

If you’re a “trader,” Etsy displays your trader status, business registration number, your business’s location, and your business’s address (only if it’s different from your personal home address). You can add other information required by local laws in the Other details box in your Seller details section.

Learn more about the EU Omnibus Directive and how to update the information Etsy displays. 

Cancellations

Set a shop-wide cancellation policy to let buyers know whether or not you accept cancellations after they place an order. 

To edit your current policy:  

  1. Select the pencil icon next to your current policy. If you have not yet made a policy, select the Create Policy button instead. 
  2. In the Edit policy field, toggle cancellations on or off.
  3. Select the time frame that you'll accept cancellations. 
  4. Select Publish. 

Privacy policy

Select Create a policy to share how you’ll protect a buyer's personal data. If you’re unsure what to write, you can use our sample privacy policy and customize it for your shop. Once your policy is finished, select Publish. 

If you're a seller based in the EU or offer items to buyers there, you’re required to create and comply with a privacy policy that satisfies the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Many other countries have also adopted data protection laws similar to the GDPR, so whether or not you sell to Europe, we recommend that all sellers create a privacy policy. Read Etsy’s Privacy Policy for more information about your obligations when collecting and using a buyer’s information, including the requirement to obtain a buyer’s consent before using their information for marketing purposes.

If you need help understanding your obligations under the GDPR or any other data protection laws, consult with an attorney about local laws and how they apply to your shop. 

Fixed policies 

You can view Etsy’s preset delivery policies for Estimated delivery dates, Customs and import taxes, and Instant downloads for digital items from this tab. These policies apply shop-wide and are not editable by sellers.

What isn’t included in shop policies?

Copyright & Intellectual Property Information

Copyright, intellectual property, or other licensing information is likely specific to an item, not to a shop. You may choose to put this information in your FAQs.

Sales tax

Etsy offers sellers a tax tool to help you calculate and display the appropriate tax rate to buyers at Checkout. There's no need to list this information in your policies, especially because tax rates vary based on the location of the buyer.

When can I edit my shop policies?

You can edit your shop policies whenever you like. A time stamp will show the last time your policies have changed. When a buyer makes a purchase, they’ll see a copy of your shop policies as of the time of purchase in their receipt email.

results.name: What Does Etsy Remit to Canadian Tax Authorities?
results.title: What Does Etsy Remit to Canadian Tax Authorities?
results.body:
Due to updated Canadian tax regulations, marketplaces like Etsy may be required to collect and remit tax - including GST/HST, QST, and PST - to the relevant Canadian tax authorities on items purchased by buyers in Canada, and on fees charged to Canadian sellers in certain circumstances. 

Starting July 1, 2022, Etsy began collecting GST/HST on eligible orders placed by shoppers in Canada. Etsy automatically includes the tax in the buyer’s total at the last stage of the checkout process. Etsy is then responsible for remitting it to the relevant tax authorities.

See Canada’s government website for more information on these new tax requirements.

Jump to a section: 

  • Do I need to register for Canadian tax IDs? 
  • What tax does Etsy collect from Canadian buyers to remit to the tax authorities?
  • When does Etsy collect taxes from Canadian buyers? 
  • What is the tax on seller fees?
  • How do I enter my Canadian taxpayer IDs? 
  • How do I find the amount Etsy remits?

Do I need to register for Canadian tax IDs? 

Canadian tax regulation requires sellers to register for a GST/HST ID and to collect and remit the tax to the CRA once they’ve reached $30,000 CAD in sales. 

Sellers who have not met this threshold may not be required to register for a Canadian Tax ID, but should make the decision for themselves on whether it makes sense for their business. 

The provinces of Quebec, Manitoba, Saskatchewan and British Columbia also have their own tax rules. 

If you need help registering for GST/HST or any other taxes, or have other questions on your tax obligations, please reach out to your tax and legal advisor. 

What tax does Etsy collect from Canadian buyers to remit to the tax authorities?

Etsy will not collect and remit these taxes from Canada buyers for sales of physical goods. You should adjust your listing prices to collect any required taxes, then remit it to the appropriate tax authorities with your GST/HST or your QST filing.

By adding your GST/HST ID or QST to your Etsy account, you’re letting us know you’re already handling the taxes you're responsible for. This will prevent your buyers from being charged taxes twice.

If you are selling goods from Canada, Etsy will automatically collect GST/HST from your Canadian buyers and QST from your Quebec buyers when they purchase physical goods and will remit these taxes to the tax authorities.

If you’re already collecting and remitting this, it may result in buyers being charged taxes twice, where both you and Etsy collect taxes and remit them. 

When does Etsy collect taxes from Canadian buyers?

Etsy will start collecting tax on relevant purchases from Canadian buyers from 1 July 2022 in the followings scenarios:

Seller Tax ID Status When are buyers charged? 

GST/HST ID added to account

If the item is being shipped from a seller in Canada to a buyer in Canada, the seller will automatically include GST/HST in the listing price. 

No GST/HST ID added 

GST/HST will be charged at checkout where:

  • a physical item will be shipped from a seller in Canada to a buyer in Canada.
  • A digital item is sold to a Canadian buyer from a non-Canadian seller.

QST ID added to account

If the item is being shipped from a seller in Canada to a buyer in Quebec, the seller will automatically include QST in the listing price. 

No QST ID added 

QST will be charged at checkout where:

  • A physical item will be shipped from a seller’s Canadian address to a buyer’s Quebec address.
  • A digital item is sold to a buyer in Quebec, from sellers outside Quebec.
British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST)*

PST will be charged at checkout on all physical items and digital downloads delivered to buyers in British Columbia from locations in Canada. 

Saskatchewan Provincial Sales Tax (PST)* 

PST will be charged at checkout on all physical items and certain digital downloads delivered to buyers in Saskatchewan. 

Manitoba Retail Sales Tax (RST)*

RST will be charged on physical items and certain digital downloads delivered to buyers in Manitoba.  

*Etsy is required by law to collect these taxes from your buyers in Manitoba, Saskatchewan and British Columbia and remit it to the local tax authorities, regardless of whether you have a registered tax ID from these provinces. Where the seller is GST/HST registered, Etsy may collect slightly less PST/RST/QST on physical goods to take into consideration the GST that the seller has already included in the listing price. Where the seller is QST registered but not GST/HST registered, you may notice that Etsy will charge slightly less GST on physical goods to taken into consideration the QST that the seller included in the listing price.

Etsy will only charge the buyer taxes on items if they are ordinarily applied to the item in these regions, assuming that it has been listed correctly. For example, Etsy will not tax children's sized clothing in British Columbia, since it is not ordinarily subject to PST there.

What is the tax on seller fees?

The new Canadian regulations also require marketplaces to collect tax on the fees charged to sellers. The tax charged will depend on where the seller is located, and in some cases whether or not the seller is GST/HST or QST registered. Any taxes collected on your seller fees will be remitted by Etsy to the relevant tax authority. 

If Etsy has already collected GST/HST on the order, you won’t be charged GST/HST on order-related fees (payment processing and transaction). GST/HST will always be charged on all other seller fees such as listing fees, Etsy Ads or Offsite Ads fees, or Pattern subscription fees regardless of registration status. 

You’ll see the tax you pay on your fees reflected in your shop payment account.

Seller Taxable Status

What Will I Be Charged? 

Seller is GST/HST Registered

GST/HST will be charged on all seller fees. 

Seller is not GST/HST Registered

GST/HST will not be charged on payment processing and transaction fees for the sale of an item that Etsy already charged the buyer GST/HST on.

GST/HST will be charged on all other seller fees.

Quebec Seller is QST Registered

QST will be charged on all seller fees

Quebec Seller is not QST Registered

QST will not be charged on payment processing and transaction fees for the sale of an item that Etsy already charged the buyer QST on.

QST will be charged on all other seller fees.

Seller in British Columbia

PST will be charged on all seller fees

Seller in Manitoba or Saskatchewan

PST will not be charged on any seller fees

 

If Etsy charges you tax on your seller fees, speak with your tax accountant to find out if you can reclaim that tax from your local tax authorities.

How do I enter my Canadian taxpayer IDs? 

Follow these steps to add your Canadian taxpayer IDs to your account: 

  1. On Etsy.com, open your Shop Manager.
  2. Select Finances
  3. Choose Legal and tax information
  4. Enter your taxpayer ID(s) under Canadian Taxpayer IDs
  5. Select Submit to Etsy

  1. On Etsy.com, open your Shop Manager.
  2. Select Finances
  3. Choose Legal and tax information
  4. Under Additional taxpayer identification, choose Add info
  5. Select the type of ID you’re adding from the dropdown
  6. Input your taxpayer ID
  7. Select Submit 

Double check that you’re entering your ID in the correct field. Submitting it in the wrong field (such as putting GST in the QST field) will result in an error.

How do I find the amount Etsy remits?

You can find the sales we report to Canada by downloading your Orders CSV file.

To use your Orders CSV to see the amounts:

  1. Open Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Settings.
  3. Choose Options.
  4. Select the Download Data tab.
  5. Select Orders as the type.
  6. Choose the year but leave the month blank.
  7. Download and open the CSV. 
  8. Look for and sort the Buyer Country column.
  9. Add the Processing Fee and Order Net columns for sales that were completed by buyers in Canada.

If you have any canceled orders from Canadian buyers, you should also count those.

To find your canceled orders:

  1. Open Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Orders & Shipping.
  3. Choose the Completed tab.

Select Canceled under the Completed status on the right.

results.name: How to Track Your Progress Toward Becoming a Star Seller
results.title: How to Track Your Progress Toward Becoming a Star Seller
results.body:
Star Seller eligibility is reviewed on the 1st of every month. If you meet the criteria, it may take up to 24 hours for your badge to appear. You can see how close you are to earning Star Seller in Customer service stats.

Jump to a section:

  • Access your Customer service stats
  • Message response rate
  • On-time shipping & tracking
  • Average review rating
  • Orders
  • Sales

Access your Customer service stats

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select the Customer service stats tab.
  3. You’ll see your Customer service stats which refresh daily, as well as a monthly overview of your customer service performance at the top of the page.

  1. Sign in and go to More.
  2. Select Customer service stats under Performance.
  3. You’ll see your Customer service stats which refresh daily, as well as a monthly overview of your customer service performance at the top of the page.

Using this dashboard, you can track your daily progress across all the areas related to delivering stellar customer service. You can also track your progress toward earning individual Star Seller badges for message response rate, on-time shipping & tracking, and average review ratings. 

The overview first displays your current review period performance, which counts toward the next badge evaluation. Select the previous review period tab to view the three-month period used to determine your current badge status.

Learn more about how Star Seller metrics compare to customer service standards.

Message response rate

The Message response rate section of your Customer service stats shows information about your response time in Messages. 

You’ll see the percentage of messages that received a response to the initial message within 24 hours. “Initial message” means the first message in a single conversation with a buyer, also known as a “thread.” You must respond to 95% of all your initial messages within 24 hours to qualify for Star Seller and receive the "Speedy replies" badge.

Message response rate is calculated by dividing the number of new messages you’ve responded to within 24 hours by the total number of new messages you've received during the calculation period.

Messages sent on the last 2 days of the 3-month review period may be excluded from the current review period and counted toward the next period instead. This is to allow sellers a full 24 hours to respond and not be penalized for messages received late on the final day of the review period.

The Message response rate only applies to the first message in a thread with a buyer. 

To help keep track of messages you should prioritize for Star Seller metrics, notification badges are displayed on messages when: 

  • A buyer’s first time contacting you
  • You receive a new help with order request

Both of these types of messages need to be responded to in 24 hours to be counted positively toward your Star Seller score.

If you don’t receive any messages during the review period, the message response rate won’t be counted toward your Star Seller eligibility. You can still become a Star Seller based on the other Star Seller criteria.

Once you receive an initial message, the message response rate is applied toward your Star Seller eligibility, so be sure to reply within 24 hours.

Marking a message as unread after you’ve replied to it doesn’t restart the 24-hour response time window and doesn’t make the message you’ve replied to “new” again.

Messages marked as spam don’t count toward your response rate.

If you can’t respond to a new message thread within 24 hours, you have a few options: 

  • You can set up an Auto-reply. These are counted in your message response rate.
  • Use Quick Replies to respond quickly to questions you get commonly asked.
  • Download the Sell on Etsy app to respond to messages on the go.
  • Go on Vacation Mode if you’re taking a break from selling on Etsy. 

Before putting your shop in Vacation Mode, reply to any first messages from buyers that you’ve received, since these will affect your message response rate.

On-time shipping & tracking

The On-time shipping & tracking section shows the percentage of orders shipped on time according to the processing times you set in your listing description. You can also see a breakdown of your shop’s shipping performance. Shipping at least 95% of your orders on time with tracking will earn you the "Smooth shipping" badge. Learn more about how to set processing times and “ship by” dates.

Orders of a certain value need to have tracking or a shipping label purchased on Etsy. The requirement values are based on currency. 

 

We use the total value of the items purchased before any discounts, not including shipping and taxes.

On-time shipping & tracking will be reviewed on sales of physical items only. Digital download orders aren’t taken into account for on-time shipping & tracking for Star Seller, but will still count toward your other metrics. If you’re listing a made-to-order or custom digital item, follow the steps in our guide to ensure that your listing is accurately listed as a digital item.

Tracking may not be visible for one of these reasons: 

  • The shipping carrier may not be supported on Etsy. If Etsy cannot process your carrier’s tracking events, consider using an alternate carrier.
  • The number entered is not the tracking number, or a slight error was made in entering the number. 
  • There may be an occasional technical issue beyond your control. On-time shipping metric won’t recognize tracking added after the shipping date, and orders older than 3 months will not count toward Star Seller metrics.

Orders that don't have tracking because they are delivered or picked up in person are considered shipped without tracking, and do not meet the Star Seller criteria for shipping. 

Average review rating

In the Ratings section, you can see your shop’s rating average for reviews over a period of time. The goal is for your completed orders to have an average rating of 4.8 stars during the review period. This will earn you the "Rave reviews" badge, and get you one step closer to Star Seller.

Orders

Changing your shop currency results in a reset of your order and sales progress for the month. Adjust currency settings only if it’s absolutely necessary.

The Orders section shows the number of orders you have completed within a Star Seller review period.

To be a Star Seller, you need to have received and fulfilled at least 5 orders within a review period. Orders that are canceled are not counted toward Star Seller. This section won't appear in your dashboard if you've already met the 5-order minimum. 

Sales

The Sales section calculates the sales you made within the latest review period. This doesn't include shipping or any additional taxes collected. The items sold must meet certain thresholds, shown in the table below, within a review period. Canceled orders aren’t counted. This section won’t appear in your dashboard if you have already met the sales criteria.

results.name: How Do Etsy’s Listing Image Requirements Apply to My Listings?
results.title: How Do Etsy’s Listing Image Requirements Apply to My Listings?
results.body:
Listing images should accurately represent the items you're selling so buyers know what to expect when they make a purchase.

Etsy requires at least one unedited photo for most items. For other images, you can use photo editing tools, including AI, as long as your images accurately represent what buyers will receive.

Learn more about Listing Image Requirements.

Jump to a section:

  • What counts as an unedited photo?
  • Does every listing photo need to be unedited?
  • Can I use AI to edit my listing photos?
  • What is Etsy’s policy on AI-generated art or products?
  • What if I sell digital downloads or personalized items?
  • What happens if Etsy detects AI-generated images when I’m creating a listing?
  • What happens if someone reports my listing for potentially misusing AI?

What counts as an unedited photo?

An unedited photo should show the actual item against a real background and must not be edited or changed in any way. Some exceptions may apply depending on the types of items you sell. All your listing photos must accurately represent what the buyer will receive. Outside of your required unedited photo, you can use photo-editing tools, including AI, to adjust lighting or color, crop or resize images, or change backgrounds, as long as those edits don’t make the item appear different.

Does every listing photo need to be unedited?

For most items, you only need at least one real, unedited photo of your item against a real background. You can use photo editing tools in your other listing photos, as long as the edits don't misrepresent what buyers will receive.

Make your first listing photo the clearest, most realistic representation of the item buyers will receive. Because it’s the first image buyers see, take extra care to make sure it accurately represents your item and isn’t misleading.

Can I use AI to edit my listing photos?

Apart from your unedited photo, you can use AI-assisted tools to crop or resize images, adjust lighting or color, or change backgrounds. These edits are allowed as long as they accurately represent your item. Don’t use AI to hide damage or change an item's appearance in a way that could mislead buyers.

What is Etsy’s policy on AI-generated art or products?

Etsy has long supported new technologies that help people bring their ideas to life, as long as human creativity remains central to the process. That's why we allow AI-generated art when sellers play a clear creative role in what they create and are transparent about their process. Sellers must still disclose when an item is created using AI and cannot misrepresent AI-generated work as handmade or entirely their own creation. Learn more.

What if I sell digital downloads or personalized items?

Requirements may differ depending on what you sell:

  • Print-on-demand items: If a production partner prints your original design on a standard base product (like a t-shirt or mug), you may use a stock photo mockup, if the stock photo’s owner has authorized its use.
  • Digital downloads: If your item has a visual component, such as a printable or template, include a preview of the actual content buyers will receive. For digital items without a visual component, you may use representative imagery, including AI-generated images, as long as it doesn't mislead buyers about what they’re purchasing.
  • Customized or made-to-order items: For customized items you make yourself, use photos of real, finished items you’ve made in the past to help buyers see the quality of your work.
  • Craft patterns, recipes, seeds, or similar items: Include at least one real, unedited photo of something made using your product. AI-generated images cannot be the only images used to show the finished result.

Learn more about requirements for specific item types.

What happens if Etsy detects AI-generated images when I’m creating a listing?

If AI-generated images are detected when you create a listing, we will provide tips to help you accurately represent your item and meet our photo expectations.

What happens if someone reports my listing for potentially misusing AI?

In the beginning, these reports will help us better understand how buyers perceive potential AI misuse and won’t result in immediate enforcement action. We’ll continue investing in detection and enforcement tools as we learn more about how AI is being used across Etsy.
