results.name: How to Offer Personalized Listings
results.title: How to Offer Personalized Listings
results.body:
Add Custom options fields to your listings so buyers can personalize the items they purchase. Personalization lets buyers tell you what they’d like customized, like a name for engraving or a special message.
For the buyer, the fields appear on the listing alongside options like color or quantity. You can see the Custom options information a buyer adds on the Orders page.

Jump to a section:

  • How to add Custom options fields to listings
  • What to include in Custom options instructions
  • How to set add-on pricing for Text box fields
  • How to photograph personalized listings
  • When to offer personalizations, variations, or custom listings

How to add Custom options fields to listings

When creating a listing, use Custom options to define the information you want buyers to provide for personalized or customized orders.

You can add up to 5 fields per listing. Each field should focus on a single detail. A simpler setup—using fewer, well-defined fields—can make it easier for buyers to complete their order and provide what you need.

  1. Sign in and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Listings and select a listing you want to add personalization to.
  3. Under Item options, go to Custom options and select Add field.
  4. Select the field type you want to add and enter the requested information.
    • Select Text box to collect information like names, dates, quotes. 
    • Select List of options to create a list of choices to select from, like fonts and thread colors. 
    • Select File upload to collect images and files from buyers.
  5. Check or uncheck This field is required. 
  6. Choose Done.

  1. Sign in and go to Listings.
  2. Select the listing you want to add personalization to.
  3. Select Custom options, then the field type you want to add and enter the requested information.
    • Select Text box to collect information like names, dates, quotes. 
    • Select List of options to create a list of choices to select from, like fonts and thread colors. 
    • Select File upload to collect images and files from buyers.
  4. Check or uncheck This field is required. 
  5. Choose Done.

To edit a field, select Edit. To delete individual fields, select Delete. 

  1. Go to Listings.
  2. Check the box next to each listing you’d like to edit. 
  3. Go to Editing Options. 
  4. Choose Change Custom options.
  5. Add or edit your fields, then select Apply.

If you enable File upload personalization, content that is submitted by buyers must comply with Etsy’s Buyer Policy. If you’re concerned about a submission, contact Support.

What to include in Custom options instructions

Clear instructions help buyers provide the details you need to complete their order. When creating fields:

  • Use clear titles that describe what buyers should provide.
  • Request one detail per field whenever possible.
  • Explain how or where the personalization will appear on the item.
  • Provide an example when helpful.
  • Include limits, such as character counts or file requirements.

Use this table to decide which field type(s) works best for your listing:

Use a Text box when buyers need to add custom text, like names, dates, or short messages.

Include: 

  • A specific field title that describes what to enter (avoid generic titles like “Personalization”)
  • Instructions explaining how or where the text will appear
  • A character limit (1–1024), based on your design 
  • Whether the field is required or optional for buyers to complete


Examples of clear, informational Text box fields for a personalized birthday card: 

  1. Title: Name
    Instructions: Enter the name you want to appear on the front of the card [Example: Clifton]
  2. Title: Age
    Instructions: Enter the number you want to appear on the front of the card [Example: 80]
  3. Title: Message for inside (optional)
    Instructions: Enter the text you would like to appear on the inside of the card

Use a List of options when buyers choose from predefined selections like font styles, design variations, or materials. 
You can include up to 30 options. Keeping your list shorter (for example, 10 or fewer options) can make it easier for buyers to choose and complete their purchase. 

Include: 

  • A field title describing the selection
  • One detail per option
  • A logical ordering, if options follow a sequence
  • Whether the field is required or optional for buyers to complete

Examples of clear, informational List of options fields for a monogrammed sweatshirt: 

  1. Title: Font style (see examples in photo)
    Options: Font 1, Font 2, Font 3, etc. 
  2. Title: Text color
    Options: Black, White, Blue, Red

Use a File upload field when buyers need to upload files, like photos, logos, or artwork.

You can add one upload field per listing. Buyers can upload up to 10 files, with a maximum size of 100 MB per file. Supported file types are .jpg, .png, .svg, .heic, and .pdf.

Include: 

  • A specific field title describing what to upload
  • The number of files
  • Labels, as needed, to identify different files when requesting multiple uploads
  • Instructions explaining what the file should show
  • Whether the field is required or optional for buyers to complete

Use labels when you need buyers to upload different files for specific purposes (for example, “Front of item” and “Back of item”). Labels help clarify what each file should show. If you don’t need different types of files, you can leave labels off and have buyers upload all files together in one place.

The required or optional setting applies to the entire file upload field, not individual labels.

If the field is marked as required, buyers must upload a file for each label before they can check out.

Example of clear, informational File upload field for a locket: 

  1. Title: Pet photos
    Number of files allowed: 2
    Label 1: Left side of locket
    Label 2: Right side of locket
    Instructions: Upload clear, well-lit photos of your pet.

How to set add-on pricing for Text box fields

You can set add-on pricing for optional Text box fields. This lets you charge buyers for text-based customizations, such as embroidery, engraving, or custom messages.

For example, if you offer embroidered names on a sweater, you can create an optional Custom options field and charge an additional $5 when a buyer enters a name.

If you use variations to charge for text-based customizations, consider switching to an optional Custom options field with add-on pricing instead. This lets buyers enter personalization details and see the add-on price in one place.

How to set an add-on price for a Text box field

Add-on pricing is only supported for optional, text-based Custom options fields. Setup and management are available on Etsy.com. Add-on prices are displayed in your shop currency automatically.

  1. Go to Shop Manager and select Listings. Select the listing you want to update.
  2. Under Item options, go to Custom options. 
  3. Select Add field, then Text box, or edit an existing text box.
  4. Mark the field as optional, then enter a price in the Add-on price field.
  5. Publish your changes.

To remove an add-on price, enter $0 in the Add-on price field and publish your changes.

Pricing requirements

Add-on prices must:

  • Be between $0.20 USD and $500 USD equivalent, based on your listing currency
  • Be entered as a numeric value

How buyers see add-on pricing

When a buyer selects a field with add-on pricing, the add-on price is automatically added to the item price. Buyers see the updated total before checkout. The total, including the add-on price, also appears in buyer receipts and order details, as well as seller order details and order management views.

How to photograph personalized listings

Listing images help buyers understand and choose personalization options. Use clear, well-organized visuals to guide buyers through their choices.

Whenever possible, show real, finished items so buyers know what to expect. You may include examples of similar personalized items you’ve previously made, especially to demonstrate options like colors or styles. Be sure to note in your description that these are examples. 

You can include mockups or digital images in additional listing photos to show personalization options. Make sure text is easy to read, with strong contrast and clear fonts. 

For personalized commercial items (such as engraved or monogrammed products), your primary image must show a finished, personalized item similar to the final product. Do not use blank product images or mockups with placeholder text (ex. “Your Text Here”) as the main image. See Listing Image Requirements for more information.

Displaying personalization options in images

When displaying personalization options in images: 

  • Clearly label each personalization option shown in your images
  • Make sure image labels match the options available in your fields 
  • Consider dedicating one image per field so buyers can easily compare choices
  • Ensure text in images has strong contrast and uses an easy-to-read font

When to offer personalizations, variations, or custom listings

Personalization (in Custom options)

  • Buyers enter custom text or information.
  • The input doesn’t impact your product inventory levels.
  • The input contains personalized details for made-to-order items.

Examples of personalization include a name to be engraved, a custom message on a card, and a preferred font or embroidery thread color for a personalized clothing item.

  • Get a buyer’s phone number: If you need a buyer’s phone number for shipping purposes, contact them via Messages.
  • Prompt a buyer to acknowledge they are ordering a digital item: Etsy has taken several steps to address buyer confusion around digital items. Items are marked as Digital Download underneath each digital listing on search results pages, and in the Item details on the listing page. On the Etsy app, buyers see Instant Download on the listing image. 

Variation

  • Buyers choose from a set list of variants of the base item.
  • Each option affects inventory, price or SKU.
  • Stock is tracked for each variation. 

Examples of variations include size, base item color, and material of a clothing item.

Custom listing

You can offer custom listings in your shop by enabling custom order requests. If a buyer requests a custom item, you can convert their request to a custom listing.

  • Buyers submit a request for a one-of-a-kind item based on their specific vision or preferences.
  • The item is for a particular buyer only, so the listing is private and created directly from the original Custom Request Message thread.

Examples of custom listings include a unique sculpture commissioned by a buyer, and a welcome sign for a wedding created to meet a buyer’s specific vision for aesthetic, materials, and more.

results.name: What is the General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR)?
results.title: What is the General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR)?
results.body:
The GPSR ensures that non-food consumer products on the EU markets are safe. GPSR puts in place specific requirements for sellers who sell into the EU markets. 

For more information about GPSR, please review our Seller Handbook article.

Who does the GPSR apply to?

Subject to forthcoming guidance, certain sellers who sell, manufacture, import, or distribute items into the European Economic Area (EEA) and are “traders” (which may include businesses and professional sellers) may fall under GPSR requirements, regardless of the seller’s location. This includes: 

  • All EU member states 
  • Iceland
  • Liechtenstein
  • Norway 
  • Northern Ireland

GPSR applies to all types of products, both physical and digital, unless they are covered by other safety regulations. GPSR does not apply to sellers who do not sell to buyers in EEA states and Northern Ireland. 

Etsy is unable to advise if you qualify as a trader or a private individual. If you’re unsure what your status is, reach out to your legal advisor for more information.

To update your trader status: 

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager.  
  2. Under Sales channels, select the pencil icon next to your shop. 
  3. In the Seller details section of your public shop, select Edit 
  4. Select your status as a Trader or a Private individual.
  5. Choose Save.

What do sellers selling into EEA states and Northern Ireland need to do for GPSR?

  1. Add an Economic Operator to your account and/or update the Manufacturers field in your listing forms.
  2. Add applicable information to the Product safety info field in your listing forms.
  3. Review the General Product Safety Regulation to determine additional updates you may need to make for your specific shop. 

Under the GPSR, products can’t be placed on the EU market unless they have an EU-based economic operator responsible for key safety tasks. If you’re a manufacturer based outside the EU, you may appoint a Responsible Person (such as an Authorized Representative) for your products in the EU.

To help you find a designated EU-based Responsible Person, Etsy has partnered with trusted third-party providers, Cert-Rep and International Associates, who offer GPSR compliance services.

What if I don’t want to sell my product in EEA states and Northern Ireland? 

You can opt out of selling your products to GPSR countries. Once you opt out, buyers in EEA States and Northern Ireland won’t be able to purchase items from your shop. 

To opt out of selling in GPSR countries: 

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and open your Shop Manager.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Choose Options. 
  4. In the Choose how you sell to GPSR states section, select if you want to exclude your Physical items from being sold in EEA countries. 
  5. If you sell Digital items, select if you want those to be unable to be sold in EEA countries.
  6. Choose Save.

results.name: Selling With Klarna Invoice
results.title: Selling With Klarna Invoice
results.body:
Etsy buyers located in Germany can receive their orders before paying for them, using Klarna Invoice.

Sellers enrolled in Etsy Payments automatically accept Klarna Invoice. If a buyer selects to pay with Klarna Invoice at checkout, they agree to pay at a later date.

However, since you’ll receive payment for the order immediately in your Etsy Payment account, you don’t need to wait for the buyer to pay with Klarna. Once the funds appear on your Payment account, you can ship the order. You’ll then receive your payment according to your disbursement schedule.

Buyers Must Pay Through Klarna for Klarna Purchases

Buyers who completed their Etsy purchases with Klarna must pay with the payment instructions that Klarna sends to them. The buyer can pay for their purchase in the Klarna app or on klarna.com. If your buyer does not pay through Klarna, they may incur unnecessary payment reminders and charges and may not be approved for future purchases by Klarna.

Please do not send the buyer your own bank information to collect payment off-Etsy via a direct bank transfer, or invoice them directly through another payment service, such as PayPal. You will receive your payment directly from Etsy into your Payment account, not from your buyer.

If your buyer accidentally sends their payment directly to you, please immediately return the payment and instruct them to pay with Klarna's payment instructions after they receive it.

If your buyer requests to pay you directly, please inform them to wait for the payment instructions from Klarna, as described below:

  • If the order is completed by you within 21 days of the sale date, the Klarna payment instructions are sent to your buyer 5 days after the completion date. This ensures that they have time to receive their purchase before receiving the Klarna payment instructions.
  • If the order is not completed by you within 21 days, the Klarna payment instructions will still be sent 22 days from the purchase date. You’ll need to work with the buyer to keep them updated on when to expect their purchase as they’ll need to notify Klarna if they need an extension to pay with the payment instructions.
  • If the order is for a digital item, the Klarna payment instructions are sent to your shopper immediately after the order is completed.

In the event that a buyer pays you directly, do not refund and cancel the Etsy order as this may be considered a violation of our policies, known as an Off-Platform Transaction. It's our goal to protect buyers and sellers by having a record of all transactions that happen through Etsy, and we want to be able to offer help to either member in the event that any issues arise with the order.

Also, please do not contact Klarna on behalf of your buyer. For privacy and security reasons, Klarna can only discuss the details of an order with the buyer, not with the seller.

Returning a Klarna order

If you and your buyer have agreed to a full or partial return via Etsy's Messages or Case System, the buyer must contact Klarna Customer Support to pause their date of payment to help prevent additional reminders and fees from Klarna.

Once you have received the return, issue the appropriate refund in Shop Manager. Once you do this, the payment instructions will be updated to reflect the new amount.

Learn more about purchasing with Klarna Invoice.

results.name: How to Add Variations to Your Listings
results.title: How to Add Variations to Your Listings
results.body:
If you offer different options for an item within the same listing, you can add those options as variations. For example, if you sell a dress with different sizes and colors, you can specify these options in that dress listing’s variations.

When a buyer purchases from you, you'll see the variations they selected in your Sold Orders, receipts, and transaction notification emails.

Jump to a section:

  • How to add variations to a listing
  • How to add photos for your variations
  • How to create custom variations
  • How to hide an option
  • How variations work for buyers
  • Can I offer variations for digital listings?
  • Should I use variations or personalization?
  • Variation limitations

How to add variations to a listing

You can add variations for up to 3 item attributes while creating or editing a listing. Separate choices like size, color, and style into distinct variations instead of combining them.

To add variations:

  1. Choose the listing you’re interested in on the Listings page.
  2. Under Item options, select Add variation.
  3. Select from the list of available variations. The variations displayed depend on the category you selected for your listing. 
  4. If you want to vary the price, quantity, processing profile, or SKU numbers for your variation, toggle those options on.
  5. Choose Done.
  6. The variations you create appear under Variations. If you chose to vary on price, quantity, processing profile, or SKU, those options appear next to the variation.

To change the price, processing profile, or quantity of a variation, check the box next to the variation(s) you want to edit, then choose Update price, Update processing, or Update quantity.

Varying on price

The price you set for each option is the total price for each version of the item, not an additional cost.

If you’re a seller outside the US and India, learn how to set up different variation prices for orders shipping domestically and internationally.

Varying on size

For measurement variations, such as length or size, choose a sizing scale. Once you select a unit of measurement, specify the options you offer.

How to add photos for your variations

If this listing varies on a visible attribute, such as color, you can add photos to show that variation.

To add photos for your variations:

  1. Find the listing you want to edit on the Listings page.
  2. Add a new photo in the Photos and video section. You can add up to ten photos.
  3. Go to Variations. Add variations, if you haven’t already.
  4. Select Manage variations.
  5. Choose the pencil icon of the variation you want to add photos to. 
  6. Toggle Link photos to this variation to on. If you have more than 20 options, you can only add photos for 20 of these options.
  7. Choose Select photo for each variation and choose the photo you want to link to that variation. Buyers see this photo when selecting the variation from your shop. 
  8. Choose Done.
  9. Choose Apply. 

How to create custom variations

To add a variation that isn't included in the default list of options, you can create a new variation. However, buyers won’t be able to filter their Etsy search results based on custom variations.

To create a new variation: 

  1. From the Item options tab, choose Manage variations. 
  2. Select Add variation. 
  3. Choose Create your own. 
  4. Enter a name for your variation, toggle if you want to link photos to it, then enter the options you want to offer. 
  5. Choose Done. 
  6. Choose Apply. You can now edit it from the Item options tab. 

How to hide an option

If you don't want an option to be viewable to buyers, edit the listing, go to Variations, and toggle off Visible. You must have at least one option visible. 

If you set the quantity for one of your options to “0”, it will appear on the listing page as Sold out.

How variations work for buyers

If you have variations on a listing, buyers must select the options they want before adding your item to their cart.

If a buyer happened to add your item to their cart before you added variations to the item, they won't be prompted to select your options when they check out.

If you subscribe to Etsy Plus, shoppers can request an email notification for when a sold out item is back in stock. Learn more about restock requests.

Can I offer variations for digital listings?

Listing variations are not currently supported for digital item listings.

Should I use variations or personalization?

Use variations when buyers are choosing from a set list of options that impact price, inventory, or SKU (like size, color, or material). 

Use personalization when buyers are adding custom details. Learn more.

Variation limitations

To help keep Etsy’s website loading quickly for buyers, some limits apply to listings with many variation options:

  • Listings with 3 variation types can have up to 2,500 option combinations.
  • Listings with 1-2 variation types can have up to 4,900 option combinations.
  • You can set unique or country-specific prices, SKUs, and quantities for up to 400 option combinations.

An option combination is a unique version of your item created by your variation choices. For example, if your listing offers 10 sizes, 25 colors, and 10 materials, it has 2,500 option combinations (10 × 25 × 10).

results.title: How to Purchase an Item On Etsy
results.body:
When you buy on Etsy, you're supporting a small business by purchasing from an individual seller.

To purchase an item on Etsy, find an item you’re looking for, add it to your cart, and complete the checkout process. This guide will help you get started. 

Did you receive an Etsy gift card? Redeem a gift card and learn how to pay with it.

Jump to a section:

  • Find what you're looking for
  • Complete the checkout process
  • After you complete your order

Find what you’re looking for

If you need a little help finding your next purchase, here are a few tips:

  • Check Editors’ Picks for items hand-picked by Etsy staffers.
  • Go to Gifts to browse giftable items for different personalities, tastes, and celebrations. Learn more about buying gifts on Etsy.
  • Use the Etsy search bar and filter for items on sale, shop location, color, and more. Learn more tips for searching on Etsy.
  • Check shops’ reviews, policies, badges, and shipping times to help guide your decision.
  • If you’re shopping for someone else, consider an Etsy gift card so your recipient can purchase exactly what they want. Learn how to buy a gift card.

What if I find items I love, but I’m not ready to buy them?

To keep track of items you love on Etsy, you can add them to your Favorites by selecting the heart icons on listings. You can also curate collections of your favorites that you can return to anytime, like shopping lists. 

Learn how to keep track of your favorite items and shops.

Complete the checkout process

Once you’ve found the perfect item, complete your purchase by checking out on either Etsy.com or the Etsy app. You can sign in or create an Etsy account, or check out as a guest.  

Learn how to use a coupon code or make an offer. 

When should I use “Buy it now”? 

Use Buy it now when you’re purchasing a single listing and you want to check out quickly. You’ll just need to add the quantity of items from the listing, verify your payment method and shipping information, and select Place your order. 

When should I use “Add to cart”? 

Choose Add to cart if you want to purchase more than one listing, apply a coupon code, or add a note to the seller with instructions.

  1. To quickly purchase a listing, select Buy it now. Otherwise, choose Add to cart.
  2. In your cart, you can Edit or Remove items, or Save for later. You can also Apply a coupon code.
  3. Select Proceed to checkout. If you have multiple items in your cart but only want to purchase one, select Check out for this shop only. 
  4. Verify your shipping address and shipping method. Select Ship to if you’d like to choose a different saved address, or add a new one. 
  5. Select Payment to verify your payment method or add a new one. If you have an Etsy gift card or credit, you can redeem it here. 
  6. Once everything looks correct, select Place your order. 

  1. To quickly purchase a listing, select Buy it now. Otherwise, choose Add to cart.
  2. Select View in your cart. Here, you can Edit or Remove items, or Save for later. You can also Apply a coupon code.
  3. Select Go to checkout. If you have multiple items in your cart but only want to purchase one, select Check out from shop. 
  4. Verify your shipping address and shipping method. Select Ship to if you’d like to choose a different saved address, or add a new one. 
  5. Select Payment to verify your payment method or add a new one. If you have an Etsy gift card or credit, you can redeem it here. 
  6. Select Proceed to checkout.
  7. Confirm your order details and select Place your order. 

  1. Add an item to your cart.
  2. In your cart, you can Edit or Remove items, or Save for later. You can also Apply a coupon code. 
  3. Select Proceed to checkout and then Continue as a guest.
  4. Enter your shipping address, verify your shipping method, and select Continue to payment. 
  5. Select your payment method. You’ll need to sign in to an existing Etsy account or create a new one if you want to use an Etsy gift card or credit. 
  6. Select Review your order. 
  7. Once everything looks correct, select Place your order. 

Learn more about using guest checkout.

Card declined? Learn more about resolving a declined card.

If you’re shopping internationally, learn how currency conversion works on Etsy.

What other information do I need to add when I check out? 

If you’re giving a gift, select Mark order as gift for options such as gift messages, a gift preview email for your recipient, and gift wrapping when available. Learn more about gift-giving on Etsy.

Are there special checkout requirements for my location? 

You may have some extra steps in the checkout process depending on where you live. 

If you're in the EEA (EU, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein) you may be asked to authenticate your payment after you select Place your order. Respond to a prompt from your card issuer and provide additional information. This may be a password, a passcode, or an answer to a question.

If your shipping address is located in India, you’re prompted to enter your phone number during checkout. Your order confirmation message is then sent to you via WhatsApp and your email. If you don’t have WhatsApp on your phone, you’ll receive the confirmation via SMS. To opt out of future order confirmation texts, select the unsubscribe link in the message.

When you download a digital item on Etsy, you give up your right to a cancellation under EU consumer laws. You’ll need to check a box to acknowledge this before completing your purchase.

After you complete your order

Etsy will send you an email for each shop you purchased from. If you have any questions about your order, be sure to reach out to your seller directly.

Find your order on your Purchases page. If you purchased as a guest without signing in, your order will appear here if you connect it to an account. Learn how to connect a guest order to an account.

Where do I find my digital purchase?

If you purchased a digital file that's available for instant download, you can download the file from your Purchases page. You’ll also receive a separate email with a link to view and download your files on Etsy. 

If you purchased as a guest, you'll find a download link in your email receipt. Learn more about downloading a digital item.

What if my order doesn’t arrive on time or has a problem?

You can shop confidently with Etsy's Purchase Protection. For qualifying orders, get a full refund if your purchase doesn’t arrive on time, arrives damaged, or doesn’t match the item description or photos.

Quick answer

The best way to get help with an order you already placed is to contact the seller:

Contact seller

If you have a question about an item, the seller is the best person to answer questions about an item. Select Message the Seller on a listing page or Contact under the seller’s photo on their shop homepage.

Select an issue for help:

Enter descriptive terms in the search bar on the top of Etsy.com to start your search. For example: “rustic blue coffee mug,” or “custom charm necklace.”

You can change the order of your search results with the Sort by option above the search results.

On the left side of every search results page, you’ll see a list of filters to narrow down your results by.

Learn more about searching on Etsy.

Learn about buying gifts on Etsy.

  1. Find the items from the shop you have a promo code for. If you’re buying items from more than one shop, your cart will be divided up by shop.
  2. Select Apply shop coupon codes.
  3. Type or paste the code into the box.
  4. Select Apply.

Your coupon code applies only to the shop that offers that coupon. Shops are run by individual sellers, who manage their own promotions. Coupon codes are available at the seller's discretion and can expire at any time.

If your payment was declined, check each of these issues:

  • Double check the card information for your order: Make sure that your billing address and expiration date are up-to-date.
  • Authorize the transaction with your bank: Your bank may flag any unexpected activity on your account. Check with your bank to see if they flagged the transaction.
  • Check that you're within your daily withdrawal limit: Most banks have limits on how much money can be charged or accessed in a single day. Your bank may require you to request a higher purchase limit to complete the transaction.
  • Register your prepaid credit card: If you're using a prepaid credit card or gift card, register your personal information with the card issuer before checking out.
  • If you're in the EEA: Check your security authentication answer. To authenticate a payment, you may need to respond to a prompt from your card issuer and provide additional information. 

If none of these solutions worked, you may need to use a different payment method.

Buyers in the US

If you don’t see the option to pay with Klarna and you’re in the US, try these steps:

  •  
    • If the order is between $250 USD and $10,000 USD you’ll need to sign in to an Etsy account or create an Etsy account to check out with Klarna.
    • Check that your region setting is correct. Check that your language is set to English, currency to USD, and region to United States. 
    • The item or order value may not be between $50 USD and $10,000 USD before discounts, shipping and taxes (unless the total is $10,000 after discounts).
    • If an item is below $50 USD, combine it with more items in your cart to total over $50 USD.
    • If you still don’t see the option to pay with Klarna, the shop may not accept Klarna installment payments at this time.
    • If Klarna declines your transaction for an order over $250.01, it may be because you didn’t pass Klarna’s credit check. In this case, you can complete your order using a different payment method.
    • You can’t use Klarna to purchase an Etsy gift card, and you can’t combine Klarna payments with an Etsy gift card.

Learn more about paying with Klarna.

Buyers in Germany

If the seller ships your order within 21 days of checkout, the Klarna invoice is sent 5 days after the date it was shipped. If the order isn’t shipped within 21 days, the Klarna invoice will be issued 22 days from your purchase date.

Please do not pay your invoice via direct bank transfer to the seller, you must pay the invoice amount to Klarna.

If your order has been cancelled and you received an invoice nevertheless, please contact Klarna first.

Buyers in the UK

If you don’t see the option to pay with Klarna and you’re in the UK, try these steps:

  • If the order is between £50 GBP and £1,000 GBP, you’ll need to sign in to an Etsy account or create an Etsy account to check out with Klarna.
  • Check that your region setting is correct. Check that your language is set to English (UK), currency to GBP, and region to United Kingdom. 
  • The item or order value may not be between £50 GBP and £1,000 GBP before discounts, shipping and taxes (unless the total is £1,000 after discounts).
  • If an item is below £50 GBP, combine it with more items in your cart to total over £50 GBP.
  • If you still don’t see the option to pay with Klarna, the shop may not accept Klarna installment payments at this time.
  • You can’t use Klarna to purchase an Etsy gift card, and you can’t combine Klarna payments with an Etsy gift card.

Learn more about paying with Klarna.

If you're not seeing the option to pay with iDEAL, make sure your default account currency is set to Euro (EUR) and your default region set to the Netherlands.

If you weren’t redirected back to Etsy after completing the transaction on your bank’s website, your order may not have completed.

Your bank account may be charged but the order won't be registered on Etsy. An automatic refund should have been processed when this occurred. These refunds typically take up to 5 business days to appear back in your bank.

If you are having trouble redeeming your Etsy gift card, check the following:

  • Make sure you’re signed into your Etsy account with the correct email address. 
  • Double-check that you’re entering the correct redemption code.
  • Check to make sure  that you haven’t already used the balance of your gift card in your Etsy account by going clicking You, then Gift card balance.

If you continue to have trouble redeeming your Etsy gift card, click I still need help and include your redemption code in your request.

My gift card balance isn’t being applied to my order

Only shops that accept Etsy Payments can accept Etsy gift cards.

To find shops that accept gift cards, search for an item on Etsy and check Accepts Etsy gift cards on the left side of the search results page.

Each seller on Etsy chooses their own payment methods and policies. Contact the seller if you have any questions about their options.

results.name: How do I Set Return Policies on My Listings
results.title: How do I Set Return Policies on My Listings
results.body:
Setting return policies on your listings clearly displays important information to your buyers, including:

  • Which items from your shop can be returned or exchanged, if any
  • The time frame that you accept returns and exchanges

You can set different return and exchange policies for each physical listing you sell in your Etsy shop, or set one specific policy across all your physical listings. Buyers will see your return policies when viewing your listings. If you’re a seller outside of the EU, you must set a return policy whenever you edit or create a new listing for a physical item, even if it is to let buyers know you do not accept returns or exchanges on that listing. Not having a return policy may result in your listings appearing lower in Etsy search. Learn more about Etsy’s Customer service standards. 

If you want to set store-wide policies for things like your cancellation and privacy policies, you can do this through your shop policies. 

Jump to a section:

  • How do I set return and exchange policies on my listings? 
  • How do I change a listing’s return policy?
  • How do I use a simple return policy?
  • Do I need to accept returns or exchanges? 
  • Can digital downloads be returned?
  • How can I accept returns for items where customization is optional? 

How do I set return and exchange policies on my listings? 

When creating or managing your listings, you have the option to create a new return policy, or to choose from one of your existing policies if you have any. We also have a simple policy template that you can choose instead of creating your own. You can also create and/or apply policies to multiple listings at once in Listings Manager.

To create a return and exchange policy through Policy settings:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager. 
  2. Navigate to Settings.
  3. Select Policy settings.
  4. Navigate to Returns and exchanges.
  5. Select the Create Policy button.
  6. Choose whether you accept returns and/or exchanges for that item by selecting the checkmark next to each option. 
  7. Select the time frame that you’ll accept returns and exchanges for that item from the dropdown menu.
  8. Select Save and apply. 
  9. Select Publish. 

If you’ve created at least one policy in the past, a suggestion to use the policy you’ve set the most on your active listings will be shown. Select Apply, or select Choose another policy to either pick from your other existing policies or create a new one.

Once a policy has been created, it can only be deleted if it is not associated with any of your active listings. 

How do I change a listing’s return policy?

To change the policy you currently have applied to a listing:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager. 
  2. Select Listings. 
  3. Select the listing whose policy you want to change.
  4. Navigate to Returns and exchanges. 
  5. Select the Change Policy button.
  6. Select from one of your other existing policies. The listing’s current policy is displayed as Applied. 
  7. If you want to create a new policy instead, choose the Create Policy button. 

You can also apply a return policy to multiple listings at once through your Listings Manager:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Select Listings.
  3. Select the listing(s) whose policy you want to change.
  4. Select Editing options.
  5. Select Change return & exchange policies.
  6. Apply an existing policy, or select Create policy to create a new policy. 

How do I use a simple return policy? 

If you choose to use the simple return policy template, the following settings are applied to your listing:

  • Buyers can return or exchange the item.
  • Buyers must return it within 30 days of delivery.
  • Buyers are responsible for any return shipping costs.* 
  • Buyers are responsible for any loss in value (as agreed upon with you) if an item isn’t returned in its original condition.* 

Choose this option by selecting Apply simple policy in the listing editor. When you are satisfied with your listing, select Publish.  

* These settings are standard on all returns and not specific to the simple return policy. 

Do I need to accept returns or exchanges? 

If you’re a seller outside of the EU, all of your physical item listings must have a return policy set so buyers know what to expect when purchasing from you. However, whether you choose to accept returns or exchanges on your listings or not is completely optional and based on your individual business needs. Not having a return policy - even if that policy is “no returns accepted” - may result in your listings appearing lower in Etsy search results. 

Consumer protection laws in the EU require some sellers to offer a minimum 14-day return policy on orders that ship to those countries. For additional information on this, review this help article on EU law regarding returns and exchanges. 

Can digital downloads be returned? 

It’s not possible to set return or exchange policies on your digital listings. If a buyer contacts you about an issue with a digital item they’ve purchased, you can still choose to resolve the issue as you see fit.  

How can I accept returns for items where customization is optional? 

If you offer an item in your shop that a buyer can choose to either purchase as-is or to customize, but only want to accept returns for non-customized or personalized orders, you can let buyers know in the FAQ section of your shop. You can also mention this in the relevant listing descriptions.

To edit your shop's FAQ:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager
  2. Select the pencil icon next to your shop name under Sales Channels. 
  3. Under Frequently asked questions, choose Add an FAQ. 
  4. Select Custom and personalized orders from the drop down. 
  5. In the Answers text box, specify that you do not accept returns of customized or personalized orders. 
  6. Select Save. 

You can also edit your Messages to Buyers to let shoppers know that you do not accept returns for customized or personalized items. Message to Buyers are included on order receipt pages and in the email buyers receive when they purchase from your shop.

results.name: How the Review System Works for Sellers
results.title: How the Review System Works for Sellers
results.body:
Buyers use Etsy’s five-star review system (⭐️ is the lowest, ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ is the highest) to review their purchases.

Jump to a section:

  • When a buyer can leave a review
  • How to see your reviews

When a buyer can leave a review

Buyers have 100 days to review an order, beginning on the delivery date or estimated delivery date. For digital items, the 100-days begins when the buyer downloads the file(s).

If your order has delivery tracking, the delivery date is when the shipping carrier marks your order as Delivered.

If your order doesn't have delivery tracking, the estimated delivery date is the purchase date + processing time + shipping days.

Learn more about when a buyer can leave a review. 

Learn how to set up or change a processing time for a listing.

When can buyers review items purchased in person? 

Reviews can only be left for items sold through Etsy. If you sell an item in-person through Square, the buyer can't leave a review on Etsy. The buyer may be able to leave a review in Square.

How to see your reviews

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select your shop name under Sales Channels.
  3. Select the star rating or scroll down to your Reviews section.

You can also download your reviews into a JSON file. 

To see your reviews on the Etsy Seller app, tap More. Then under Shop, select Reviews. 

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Go to Settings and then Options. 
  3. Select Download data. 
  4. Select Download Your Reviews. 

What does my review score mean? 

Your score is a recency-weighted average of all the star ratings you've received. Reviews from the past 12 months are given the most weight, to best reflect your recent item quality and customer service. While each rating keeps its original star value, the weight it carries in the average calculation decreases by half each year.

You're welcome to respond to buyer reviews.

Can other buyers see review photos or videos?

If a buyer includes a photograph or video in their review, this will be visible to anyone who looks at your reviews.

What if I receive an inappropriate review?

If you feel as though the review, or its photo or video, is in violation of our policies, please select Report this Review directly under the review. Learn what to do if you receive a negative review.

Etsy employees may remove reviews that violate Etsy’s policies or guidelines. Reviews or comments which are removed by Etsy employees cannot be reinstated.

results.name: What Information Does Etsy Report for Sellers in the EU, UK, and Canada?
results.title: What Information Does Etsy Report for Sellers in the EU, UK, and Canada?
results.body:
Under EU, UK, and Canadian law, online marketplaces like Etsy are required to:

  • Provide details of EU sellers and their transactions to EU tax authorities annually. This reporting requirement is commonly referred to as DAC 7.
  • Provide details of UK sellers and their transactions to HMRC (His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs). This reporting is referred to as the Model Rules for Reporting by Platform Operators (UK MRDP).
  • Provide details of Canadian sellers and their transactions to Canadian Revenue Agency (CRA). This reporting is referred to as the Canada Reporting Rules for Digital Platform Operators.

Jump to a section:

  • When is Etsy required to send EU, UK, and Canadian seller information to relevant tax authorities?
  • What seller data is Etsy required to report?
  • What if my reported information is incorrect?

When is Etsy required to send EU, UK, and Canadian seller information to relevant tax authorities?

Etsy is required to send EU, UK, and Canadian seller information to relevant tax authorities when:

  • You complete 30 or more transactions in a calendar year with physical goods

Or 

  • You make €2,000 (EU) (circa GBP £1,700) / CAD $2,800 (Canada) or more on physical goods sales after taxes and fees in a calendar year

Or

  • You make any sales of made-to-order digital items (custom files made to a buyer’s specification that will be sent to them upon completion) in a calendar year

Sellers who don’t meet the above thresholds within the tax year are exempt from reporting. 

What seller data is Etsy required to report?

The information that Etsy is required to share with tax authorities depends on whether you’re registered as an individual or a business entity.

Etsy is legally required to collect and verify the information below to report to tax authorities in order to comply with regulations. Please review and update your tax information to make sure it’s accurate for reporting. 

If Etsy reaches out to you to request your information, but you don’t provide it within the specified timeframe on the email, Etsy will put your shop on pause via Vacation Mode. This means you won’t be able to receive new orders, and your listings won’t appear in search results on Etsy until you confirm your information.

I’m registered as an individual 

Etsy is required to report:

I’m registered as a business entity 

Etsy is required to report:

Financial data collected

Etsy is also obligated to share information on seller’s transactions with tax authorities. You’re provided with a PDF summary that shows the information Etsy reported to the tax authorities by January 31 of each year. The information includes: 

  • Total number of transactions completed during the period. 
  • Total amount paid or credited to the seller during each quarter of the period. The total amount paid is your total gross sales minus any refunds, fees, and Etsy-remitted taxes.*
  • Total amount of fees, commissions, or taxes withheld or charged by Etsy during each quarter of the period. 

* Consideration will include sales of physical items as well as the sale of made-to-order digital downloads. This does not include instant download digital files that the buyer can access immediately upon purchase.

What if my reported information is incorrect?

If you meet the threshold for reporting, you will receive notifications via email and Shop Manager prompting you to review, update, or supply any missing taxpayer details. Ensure the accuracy and currency of your information on the Legal and tax information page for reporting reasons.

Learn more about how to update your legal name and taxpayer information. If any reported information is inaccurate, contact Etsy Support.

results.name: How to Add Tracking and Complete an Order
results.title: How to Add Tracking and Complete an Order
results.body:
Quick answer

Buyers are typically notified that their items are on their way based on the ship date you set when purchasing a shipping label and completing your orders. If you purchased an Asendia, Evri, Fedex, USPS (excluding letters/flats), or UPS shipping label through Etsy, your buyer will be notified after the carrier scans their package.

Make sure that the ship date matches the date you plan to hand off the order to the shipping carrier. 

There are 2 ways to add tracking to an order: 

  • Purchase shipping labels on Etsy. If you use shipping labels purchased on Etsy, tracking is automatically included.
  • If you complete an order without purchasing a shipping label, tracking information can be added manually.

When you add tracking to your order or use shipping labels purchased on Etsy, you help provide your buyer an excellent customer service experience by keeping them updated about the status of their shipment. Adding tracking information is required to complete an order for US sellers.

Jump to a section:

  • How do I add tracking and complete an order on Etsy.com?
  • When is a tracking number required?
  • How do I accurately complete my orders?
  • How do I edit the tracking number on an order?
  • How do I add tracking information after completing an order?
  • How do I combine multiple orders into one shipment and complete them?

How do I add tracking and complete an order on Etsy.com?

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Shop Manager and then Orders.
  2. In the New tab, you'll see a list of your sales that you haven't completed yet.
  3. Select the Update progress icon on the right side of the order you're interested in.
  4. Select Complete order.
  5. Choose a Ship date. You can choose to set a Ship date up to 3 days in the future. We will not send a Shipping Notification to your buyer until the package’s Ship date, or, depending on the carrier, until after the package is scanned. Ship dates are based on Eastern Time.
  6. Add a personal Note to buyer. You can save up to 10 versions of your Note to buyer. To save a note, write your message in the Note to buyer field. Then select Add to saved notes.
  7. Select a Shipping carrier and add a Tracking number.
  8. Select Preview buyer notification to view the shipping notification that will be sent to your buyer. If you’d like, check Email me a copy of this notification.
  9. Select Complete order.

  1. On the Etsy Seller app, go to your Orders tab. 
  2. Select the order you're looking to complete from your list. 
  3. Review the order information and select Complete order. 

  4. Put in your order’s tracking number. If your order doesn't have tracking, such as if it’s a digital item or an item for local pickup, select This order doesn’t have tracking and choose your reason from the list of options.

  5. Choose your Shipping carrier from the dropdown menu. 
  6. Select a date from the Ship date dropdown. You can choose to set a Ship date up to 3 days in the future. Buyers won't receive a shipping notification until the package’s Ship date,  or, depending on the carrier, until after the package is scanned. Ship dates are based on Eastern Time.
  7. Select Add note to buyer to include a personalized message and choose Save. Select the pencil icon if you need to edit your message. 

  8. Select the checkmark if you would like to have a copy of this notification emailed to you.

  9. Select Complete order.

When is a tracking number required? 

Orders for physical items must have a valid tracking number in order for them to qualify towards Star Seller. You may risk losing your Star Seller badge if you ship orders without including tracking. 

Orders must also have valid tracking to qualify for Etsy Purchase Protection. If something goes wrong with a qualifying order, Etsy Purchase Protection can help you keep your earnings from that sale.

Tracking is not required in the following instances: 

  • Digital downloads, including custom digital items
  • Customized order additions linked to another order
  • Orders being delivered through local pickup
  • The shipping of oversized and heavy items

If you need to indicate an exception other than what is listed, you’ll see an option to indicate This order doesn't have tracking below the tracking number field. You can then add a quick explanation for why you can’t add tracking for an order.

How do I accurately complete my orders? 

When you complete an order, either when you purchase a shipping label from Etsy or are completing it manually, you must set a ship date for when you expect to hand the item over to the shipping carrier. Depending on your shipping method, an email may be automatically sent to the buyer letting them know their order is in transit on the ship date you set. If you purchased an Asendia, Evri, Fedex, USPS (excluding letters/flats), or UPS shipping label through Etsy, the email will be sent after the carrier has scanned the package.

If you set a ship date for an order before the package is actually en route, it creates an inaccurate expectation of when the buyer will receive it. This can also cause your order to arrive later than its estimated delivery date, which can impact things like your on-time delivery rate for Star Seller, or the order’s eligibility for Etsy Purchase Protection.

How do I edit the tracking number on an order? 

Once you complete an order and add tracking information manually, you have 3 days to make changes to the tracking number or shipping carrier.

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Shop Manager, then Orders.
  2. Select Completed.
  3. Choose the order with the tracking information you want to change and scroll down to the package you want to edit.
  4. Select Edit tracking next to the original tracking number.
  5. Make any changes to the tracking number or shipping carrier.
  6. Select Save. 

If you need to change the number after 3 days, you can contact your buyer through Etsy Messages with the correct tracking number, and add the tracking number to your private notes on the order for your records. Keeping your buyer updated will help avoid any potential confusion or disputes.

How do I add tracking information after completing an order?

After you complete an order, you can add tracking information at a later date.

To add a tracking number to a completed order:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to Shop Manager, then Orders.
  2. Select Completed.
  3. Select the ... icon next to the order you want to add tracking information to.
  4. Select Add a package.
  5. From here you can:
    • Choose a Ship date. You can choose to set a Ship date up to 3 days in the future. We will not send a Shipping Notification to your buyer until the package’s Ship date. Ship dates are based on Eastern Time.
    • Add a personal Note to Buyer.
    • Add a tracking number, if one was provided by your shipping carrier. If you already added a tracking number to the order previously, this new tracking number will appear on the order in addition to the previous number(s) you have entered.

How do I combine multiple orders into one shipment and complete them?

If a buyer purchases several items from your shop that you can combine into one shipment, you can complete the orders in the following ways: 

Combining multiple orders into one box:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Go to Orders.
  3. Find one of the buyer’s orders you want to buy a shipping label for.
  4. Select the icon of a van to purchase a shipping label.

  6. Finish purchasing your shipping label. 
  7. Complete the order as usual. 
  8. Copy the tracking number for the combined package. 
  9. Find the other purchases from the buyer’s order and select the Complete order icon. 
  10. Paste the combined package’s tracking number into the Tracking number field. 
  11. Fill out the rest of the information and select Complete order. 
  12. Repeat this process for each item in the combined order.
  13. Refund the extra shipping costs for the additional orders back to the buyer.

If you have orders that you shipped, but that are still in the New tab of your orders page, you may need to select Complete order.

To complete an order, find the order on your Orders & Shipping tab. Select the timer icon on the order, then choose Complete order.

  • Add a tracking number, if one was provided by your shipping carrier.

This review may take up to 72 hours, although it may occasionally take longer. This review process is in place to protect you and other sellers and buyers on Etsy from possible fraud.

The buyer has also received an email letting them know that their order is being reviewed by Etsy.

Once the order has fully processed, both you and the buyer will receive an email confirmation. Please don’t take any further action regarding your order until you receive the confirmation email.
